

WL-REQ-1867 fixes the wire form. `GET /api/v1/docs/{id}`, `/rules/{id}` and
`/tasks/{id}` with `?as=blocks` (`internal/api/docs.go`, `rules.go`,
`tasks.go`) add `blocks`, built with `mdblocks.Parse(body, Subject(kind))`,
and `body_sha256`, the hex SHA-256 of the stored body, to the response;
without the parameter the response is unchanged. `model.BlocksBody` becomes
`{Blocks []EditorBlock, BodySHA256 string}` and is embedded in each response
type with `omitempty`. The body writes (`PATCH /api/v1/docs/{id}`,
`PUT /api/v1/rules/{id}`, `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{id}`) accept `blocks` in
place of `body`: a write carrying both is `422`; a blocks write runs
`EditorBlock.Validate` on each block, then `mdblocks.Write`, and continues
down the existing Markdown path (so normalisation and inline references
apply). Response on a blocks write is the same as on a Markdown write.

Each touched route gets its `routeDoc` updated (request body alternatives,
`422` for both fields or an invalid block type), and each route's `*Params`
struct gains `As string` (`query:"as"`, only `blocks` accepted). `internal/cli` gets `Client` methods the
part-2 tests and the e2e test use; no new `lode` verb (agents write
Markdown).

```go
func TestRuleReadAsBlocks(t *testing.T) {
    srv, tok := newTestServer(t)
    id := mustCreateRule(t, srv, tok, "## H\n\npara\n")
    var got model.BlocksBody
    getJSON(t, srv, tok, "/api/v1/rules/"+id+"?as=blocks", &got)
    if len(got.Blocks) != 2 || got.Blocks[0].Type != "heading" || got.Blocks[1].Type != "paragraph" {
        t.Fatalf("got %+v", got.Blocks)
    }
    if sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("## H\n\npara\n")); got.BodySHA256 != hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) {
        t.Fatalf("body_sha256 = %q", got.BodySHA256)
    }
}
```
